Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (in no particular order). These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have been praised for their storytelling, performances, and atmospheric tension.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Night Comes for Us** | Timo Tjahjanto | Joe Taslim, Baim Wong | A hyper‑stylized Indonesian action‑thriller that blends brutal violence with a compelling revenge narrative. Its kinetic choreography and relentless pacing earned it cult‑status among genre fans. |
| 2 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that reimagines the classic horror premise as a tense cat‑and‑mouse chase. Moss’s performance and the film’s smart use of technology make it a standout. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s signature blend of sharp dialogue, slick visuals, and a complex plot about drug‑dealers and corporate takeovers keeps viewers guessing until the end. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish drama that turns into a tense thriller when a group of men falsely accuse a man of child abuse. The film’s moral ambiguity and strong ensemble cast create a gripping narrative. |
| 5 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | Though more historical drama than pure crime‑thriller, its courtroom showdown and exploration of truth vs. perception give it a thrilling edge. |
| 6 | **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Riley Keough | A bleak, atmospheric tale of crime and corruption in rural America. The film’s dark tone and strong ensemble performances deliver a slow‑burn thriller experience. |
| 7 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller. Sorkin’s razor‑sharp script and the film’s real‑world relevance keep audiences on edge. |
| 8 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | While primarily a gangster epic, its investigative structure and use of de‑scalation techniques create a suspenseful narrative arc. |
| 9 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish sci‑fi thriller that uses a vertical prison setting to explore social inequality. Its claustrophobic atmosphere and moral dilemmas make it a tense watch. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that reimagines the classic horror premise as a tense cat‑and‑mouse chase. Moss’s performance and the film’s smart use of technology make it a standout. |

### How to Watch

- **Streaming**: Many of these titles are available on major platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, and HBO Max. Check your local streaming catalog for availability.
- **Rent/Buy**: Digital rental or purchase options are typically available on iTunes, Google Play Movies, and YouTube Movies.
- **Physical Media**: Blu‑ray/DVD releases can be found on Amazon or specialty retailers like Best Buy.

Enjoy diving into these gripping crime‑thrillers!
